- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., < 0.33) and model shows gradual upward drift, reduce forecast slope; price may not rebound as expected.
- If model forecasts a steady upward trend after a sharp spike, check for overconfidence — true price often corrects downward after peak.
- In high-event periods (e.g., >15 events/30d, net supply negative), model tends to overestimate price rise; apply downward bias correction.
- If sentiment is bullish but price drops sharply (e.g., 5–10% from peak), model may be lagging — adjust for recent volatility.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model often overestimates mean reversion — price may stay volatile longer than forecast.
- In multi-auction periods (e.g., CAP3 EU + DE), model tends to underestimate supply shock — add 2–5% downward adjustment for auction-driven supply events.
- If model shows linear trend with no volatility, true price often exhibits mean reversion or sudden drops — add volatility buffer or stochastic adjustment.
- For long-term forecasts (30d), if sentiment is bearish and model is flat, consider downward drift — price may fall 3–5% below forecast baseline.
